cards.power: Block 1 attack, but permanently reduce your Max Health.
cards.lore: The illusion of safety only delays the beating. Innocence must be sacrificed to gain wisdom. To refuse is to remain a victim.
cards.gradeReason: Protection-as-trap is instantly embodied. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: small puppy hiding under torn blanket while giant bear looms. Mood: false security.

cards.power: Shift damage to a teammate. Gain +1 Cowardice.
cards.lore: Moral weakness demands you refuse responsibility. Maturation demands you look in the mirror.
cards.gradeReason: Blame-shifting cowardice is universally legible. Players know exactly what to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: opossum pointing frantically at teammate while referee watches. Mood: defensive deflection.

cards.power: Ignore all ring effects this turn. You cannot attack.
cards.lore: The Mask is a survival mechanism that worked once, and is now your trap.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp concept but wrestling 'gimmick' frame gates the instant read slightly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: masked character frozen mid-ring while fire burns around them. Mood: trapped by persona.

cards.power: Sacrifice 2 cards to boost the Boss's stats.
cards.lore: Loyalty to the wrong system guarantees your destruction. Find your own truth.
cards.gradeReason: Thematically clean but mechanic complexity dilutes the immediate role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: animals kneeling before golden boot trophy while arena crumbles. Mood: doomed devotion.

cards.power: Discard your Naivety tokens to gain Responsibility buffs.
cards.lore: You aren't discovering the world. You are being formed by it, violently.
cards.gradeReason: Literary reference (Bildungsroman) gates it; lore lands hard for those who catch it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: young hound being flung across ring by older competitors. Mood: violent formation.

cards.power: Deal damage equal to the number of Oppression tokens on the board.
cards.lore: The system knows best. That is the lie. Resistance is your only moral duty.
cards.gradeReason: Instantly puts player in YA resistance mode. Every teenager knows this cage.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: raccoon in dystopian arena surrounded by oppression tokens glowing red. Mood: righteous fury.

cards.power: Leave your Faction. Gain +3 Solo Power, but lose all Support cards.
cards.lore: Identity exists beyond the faction. You are not just like the others.
cards.gradeReason: Clear coming-of-age moment but requires faction mechanic familiarity to click fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: zebra walking away from crowd of identical animals, spotlight finding them alone. Mood: lonely individuation.

cards.power: Take 2 damage to draw 3 cards. Normalcy is no longer an option.
cards.lore: Talent requires sacrifice. The calling is an inescapable agony.
cards.gradeReason: Pain-for-creation is universally legible. The agony of calling is instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: peacock painting blindfolded while bleeding, canvas glowing. Mood: ecstatic suffering.

cards.power: Convert 1 Trauma token into a Barbed Wire barricade.
cards.lore: The world was never meant to protect you. Resilience is an order you build yourself.
cards.gradeReason: Trauma-as-weapon is viscerally immediate. Players know exactly what they're doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: porcupine weaving trauma tokens into barbed wire fortress. Mood: fierce self-construction.

cards.power: Change your Type to match the opponent's, avoiding damage but losing your Turn.
cards.lore: The ultimate illusion: I must adapt to be loved.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is a knockout but the specific identity framing asks players to locate themselves first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: two flamingos mid-match, one morphing to match the other's color while looking ashamed. Mood: painful accommodation.

cards.power: Play cards from two different Faction decks, but pay double the energy cost.
cards.lore: Torn between two rings. The illusion is believing you must choose only one.
cards.gradeReason: The dual-belonging double cost is mechanically brilliant and instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: chameleon halfway up ladder between two wrestling rings in different arenas. Mood: suspended belonging.

cards.power: Discard your entire hand of Career cards to draw a new hand of Desperation.
cards.lore: The second adolescence. The lie is telling yourself: I know exactly who I am.
cards.gradeReason: Universal dread. 'I know exactly who I am' as the fatal lie is a gut-punch G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: walrus in mirror surrounded by discarded career trophies, holding new empty hand of cards. Mood: desperate reinvention.

cards.power: Destroy 1 Authority card on the board. All players take 2 Chaos damage.
cards.lore: The societal structures you trusted have failed. The first safe world collapses.
cards.gradeReason: Authority collapse reads well but 'first safe world' abstraction needs a beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: raccoon in suit at burning desk, arena crumbling behind, players reeling. Mood: systemic collapse.

cards.power: Remove all Location buffs. You cannot return to your Starting Zone.
cards.lore: Loss of the home space. Protection is permanently revoked.
cards.gradeReason: Loss of home is primal and instant. 'Permanently revoked' seals the deal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: opossum with bindle outside padlocked locker room door. Mood: permanent exile.

cards.power: Your Mentor card loses all abilities and becomes a 0/1 Meat Shield.
cards.lore: The mentor is flawed, selfish, and broke. True wisdom offers no emotional comfort.
cards.gradeReason: Flawed mentor archetype is universally legible. Zero emotional comfort is a G1 knife-twist.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: elderly fox mentor in tattered suit, abilities stripped, used as human shield. Mood: disillusioned dependency.

cards.power: Opponents can cheat (play 2 cards instead of 1) this turn. No penalties.
cards.lore: The universe is not cruel. It is simply, devastatingly indifferent.
cards.gradeReason: Indifferent universe as the harshest truth. Instantly felt by everyone who's ever looked for fairness.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: zebra referee looking away while bear cheats openly, universe shrugging in background. Mood: cosmic indifference.

cards.power: Sacrifice your Ally to negate an attack targeted at you.
cards.lore: Friends will always sacrifice you for their own survival. Peer betrayal is mandatory.
cards.gradeReason: Friendship as forced sacrifice is immediately felt. 'Mandatory' makes it gut-level.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: golden retriever throwing cat teammate into attack while diving away. Mood: necessary betrayal.

cards.power: Copy the last card played by an Ally. The Ally must discard it.
cards.lore: The second safe world is a lie. Equality is just a pause before exploitation.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp lore but 'second safe world' requires the deck's narrative arc to land fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: fox copying otter's signature move while otter watches, hand now empty. Mood: casual exploitation.

cards.power: Target player cannot use Support or Faction abilities for 3 turns.
cards.lore: Social excommunication. You are now a pariah in the world you helped build.
cards.gradeReason: Social death is immediately felt. 'World you helped build' twists the knife perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: animals whispering in circle excluding isolated mouse who built the gym. Mood: social annihilation.

cards.power: If you have no Allies on the board, gain +5 Base Attack.
cards.lore: The terrifying reality of individual survival. Nobody is coming to save you.
cards.gradeReason: Nobody is coming to save you. Full stop. Plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: lone figure walking spotlight entrance tunnel, empty arena, no cheering. Mood: brutal solitude.

cards.power: Reveal your hand. Take 1 damage for every Trick card you hold.
cards.lore: You must see your own hand in the disaster. The illusion of your innocence is dead.
cards.gradeReason: Moral complicity concept is strong but requires introspection that slows the immediate performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: animal covering eyes as giant screen replays their own tricks back at them. Mood: forced self-confrontation.

cards.power: Remove all ongoing effects, buffs, and debuffs from the entire board.
cards.lore: The final bastion of innocence falls. The script was a lie you chose to believe.
cards.gradeReason: The script was a lie you chose to believe. Nuclear lore. Instantly understood.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: tiger smashing mirror ring-post, scripts and illusions shattering around all players. Mood: violent disillusionment.

cards.power: Gain the Champion Token. You now take double damage from all sources.
cards.lore: Accepting the true cost of the illusion. Being the best is a life sentence.
cards.gradeReason: Strong mechanic-lore mirror but 'true cost of the illusion' needs a beat to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: gorilla wearing championship belt, visibly crushed under its weight while cheering continues. Mood: pyrrhic victory.

cards.power: Discard 2 Weakness cards to permanently upgrade your Base Stats.
cards.lore: You must overcome BOTH the need for comfort and the refusal of responsibility.
cards.gradeReason: Truby screenwriting reference is opaque; lore states the formula without making you feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: raccoon discarding comfort blanket and shield simultaneously, leveling up. Mood: double overcoming.

cards.power: Immune to Fear. Takes double damage from Reality checks.
cards.lore: Your strength IS the illusion. You only survive because you don't know the odds.
cards.gradeReason: Wrestling-specific 'jobber' term gates slightly; the lore paradox is brilliant once decoded.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: cheerful lamb skipping into ring while surrounded by warning signs it cannot see. Mood: blissful exposure.

cards.power: Force an Ally to take 1 damage, but they gain +3 Attack next turn.
cards.lore: The true Mentor offers brutal truth, absolute clarity, and zero emotional comfort.
cards.gradeReason: Brutal truth plus zero emotional comfort is a role players can immediately inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: bear in suit punching teammate while pointing at scoreboard. Mood: harsh mentorship.

cards.power: Heal 2 HP now, but lose 4 HP at the end of the turn.
cards.lore: The False Caregiver. Temporary, deceptive security from someone who lacks true power.
cards.gradeReason: False caregiver is universally legible. The delayed 4HP loss makes it physically real.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: parrot in bow tie offering bandage with hidden knife behind back. Mood: sweet deception.

cards.power: Copy an opponent's action, but apply a different outcome.
cards.lore: Same starting line, different choices. Maturation is a choice, not an automatism.
cards.gradeReason: 'Automatism' is slightly clinical; the concept is sharp but the word brakes momentum.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: bear cub mirroring older bear's stance but stepping left instead of right. Mood: conscious divergence.

cards.power: Tax every card played by opponents (costs +1 Energy).
cards.lore: Authority represents power vs. morals. They have their own logical, crushing gravity.
cards.gradeReason: Tax mechanic is sharp; lore 'vs.' phrasing feels like a placeholder — reads as draft copy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: rhinoceros in suit and championship belt taxing every move from ringside throne. Mood: institutional weight.

cards.power: Cannot attack on the first turn of combat. Generates 1 Pity token.
cards.lore: Adults are not evil. They are weak, compromised, and still failing to mature.
cards.gradeReason: Adults are not evil — they are weak and still failing to mature. Best reframe in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: old lion with championship scars, frozen at ring entrance, generating pity aura. Mood: failed adulthood.

cards.power: Ignore all Appeal and Promo effects this turn.
cards.lore: The World. It does not actively hate you. It just doesn't care if you die.
cards.gradeReason: It just doesn't care if you die. Lore perfection. Instantly devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: crowd of animals looking at phones while performer bleeds in ring below. Mood: cosmic boredom.

cards.power: Rearrange the top 3 cards of any deck.
cards.lore: The illusion of free will in the ring. You are wrestling someone else's thesis.
cards.gradeReason: Wrestling someone else's thesis is excellent lore; card mechanic effect is abstract.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: octopus with typewriter rearranging wrestlers like chess pieces from above. Mood: invisible control.

cards.power: Reveal your hand to your opponent. Gain 1 Trust token immediately.
cards.lore: Simplistic, trusting, authority-blind. You speak the words they gave you.
cards.gradeReason: You speak the words they gave you. Every player remembers performing this. G1 anchor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: golden retriever puppy at microphone reciting from script, crowd applauding. Mood: innocent compliance.

cards.power: Deal 2 damage to EVERYONE, including yourself.
cards.lore: Polarizing, black-and-white teen angst. You reject the script, but have no voice of your own.
cards.gradeReason: Deal damage to everyone including yourself is a mechanically perfect description of teen rage.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: angry wolverine screaming into mic, everyone in ring including self reeling. Mood: uncontrolled rebellion.

cards.power: Discard a card to cancel an opponent's card, but end your turn immediately.
cards.lore: Splintered, contradictory transition. The old voice is dead; the new one isn't born.
cards.gradeReason: Transition limbo is sharp; card has a label error ('LOWER' instead of 'LORE') — production issue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: chameleon mid-color-change at microphone, words fragmenting around them. Mood: voice in transit.

cards.power: Play two contradictory cards simultaneously without penalty.
cards.lore: Self-critical, capable of holding contradiction. You finally own your own narrative.
cards.gradeReason: Owning contradiction needs the arc to land; works best as deck closer than standalone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: owl commentator holding two opposing signs, both smiling, crowd split but listening. Mood: earned complexity.

cards.power: +5 Attack, but you lose control of your target (roll a die to select).
cards.lore: Physical maturation wildly outpaces psychoical readiness. The body becomes a trap.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic-lore match is excellent; 'psychoical' is a visible typo that undercuts the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: teenage bear massively overmuscled, swinging wildly at random targets. Mood: body outrunning mind.

cards.power: Neither player can play more than 1 card per turn.
cards.lore: Childhood space. The walls that protect you are the same walls that imprison you.
cards.gradeReason: Walls that protect are walls that imprison is strong; location framing slightly slows it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: small gym with padded walls, characters pressed together, protected but trapped. Mood: sheltered suffocation.

cards.power: Remove all Location protections. All characters take +1 damage from attacks.
cards.lore: Wide open space. Total freedom is just another word for infinite threats.
cards.gradeReason: Freedom as infinite threat is conceptually rich but indirect — needs a player willing to sit with the paradox.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: tiny animal in vast empty stadium, arrows raining from all directions with no cover. Mood: exposed freedom.

cards.power: Swap a character from your Bench with your Active character.
cards.lore: The physical threshold of psychological change. You cannot return to the locker room.
cards.gradeReason: Wrestling fans recognize Gorilla Position instantly. Threshold-of-no-return is poetic G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: gorilla standing at curtain threshold, reaching back to pull waiting character forward, no return path. Mood: threshold crossing.

cards.power: If played, opponent immediately steals this card and slaps you with it.
cards.lore: SIN: Omniscient guides. If the mentor doesn't bleed, the lesson is slop.
cards.gradeReason: If the mentor doesn't bleed, the lesson is slop. Best SIN in the deck. Instantly applies.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: wizard wand bouncing back from opponent straight into caster's face. Mood: magical self-own.

cards.power: Skip your turn to heal 1 HP.
cards.lore: SIN: The Nostalgia Trap. The past was a cage. Stop trying to climb back in.
cards.gradeReason: The past was a cage. Stop trying to climb back in. Zero-star clarity. Instantly felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: pig in rose-tinted goggles trying to squeeze back into tiny childhood cage labelled 'the good old days'. Mood: delusional nostalgia.

cards.power: Draw 5 cards, then instantly discard them all.
cards.lore: SIN: Instant wisdom without incremental pain. Real growth is paid in installments.
cards.gradeReason: Draw 5, discard all — the mechanic IS the SIN. No explanation needed. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: character surrounded by light bulbs that all shatter instantly, hands empty. Mood: hollow epiphany.

cards.power: Target enemy gains +2 predictable damage but loses all Strategy options.
cards.lore: SIN: One-dimensional evil. If your adults are cartoons, your protagonist is a joke.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is a sharp critique; needs the player to be writing or reading the story to fully bite.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: rat in top hat and mustache telegraphing every move while hero yawns. Mood: lazy antagonism.

cards.power: Link two characters. When one dies, the other takes 5 damage.
cards.lore: Perfect, unwavering peer loyalty. True arcs demand betrayal from the inside.
cards.gradeReason: The lore SIN is sharp but mechanic complexity takes a beat to resolve against the concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: two meerkats signing contract in blood, chain visibly linking them, one looking nervous. Mood: sworn doom.

cards.power: Heal all damage, but permanently lose the ability to Win the game.
cards.lore: SIN: The 'Happy Maturation' reward. Growing up is a loss. It costs something irreversible.
cards.gradeReason: Heal all damage but permanently lose the ability to Win. The mechanic demolishes the happy ending SIN. Perfection.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: badger celebrating with confetti surrounded by healed players, Win card visibly disintegrating. Mood: pyrrhic joy.

cards.power: Discard your current Character Card. Draw a new one with +1 to all stats.
cards.lore: Novelty Budget: You never return to who you were. You are only ever new, and scarred.
cards.gradeReason: You are only ever new and scarred is devastating lore; stat-boost mechanic cuts against the wound slightly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: fox discarding old self-card, new fox emerging with visible scars but shining slightly. Mood: irreversible becoming.

cards.power: Game Over. Tally your remaining Trauma tokens to calculate your final identity score.
cards.lore: Tension resolved. The illusion is dead. Now, who the hell are you?
cards.gradeReason: Who the hell are you? Perfect closer. No embellishment needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash cartoon. Subject: lone animal in empty arena after match, folding chair in spotlight, scoreboard blank. Mood: empty arrival.

verdict: This is the deck that actually does what coming-of-age fiction promises and rarely delivers: it puts the violence back in growing up. Structured in six thematic movements — Ring of Self-Deception, Match Types of Misery, Out-of-Ring Brawls, three Death Points, and the Cost of the Main Event — the Kayfabe Crucible reads like a field manual for surviving your own mythology. Named strength: the Disqualifications of the Hacks section is the sharpest meta-commentary on bad storytelling in this corpus; the Sudden Epiphany Bell alone is worth the price of admission. Named weakness: one opaque Truby reference and a production error on Phase 3 Stuttering Shoot ('LOWER' label) that needs correcting before print. Table-ready YES.
blurb: For anyone who survived growing up and can't quite explain the damage. A satirical card game about the violence of self-discovery — 48 cards, zero false hope.

coverQA.coverNote: This cover does the thing covers are supposed to do: it makes you pick it up. The FrizzleBob-at-drawing-board composition is a strong visual thesis statement. Sub-labels (Internal Conflict Generator, Existential Dread Amplifier, Folding Chair Symbolism) read beautifully at full size but may blur at thumbnail scale — worth checking on Gumroad preview.

notes: 2 production errors found: (1) Page 10, The Phase 3 Stuttering Shoot card has 'LOWER:' printed instead of 'LORE:' — likely a decorative font render issue where L and O merged. (2) Page 11, The Roid-Rage Growth Spurt lore contains 'psychoical' — should be 'psychological'. Page 9 credits 'Patrick Hand' as the font directly in the lore text, confirming consistent typography. No RAF dice boxes present. Decorative insect and vermin motifs in margins throughout (cockroach, bee, spider, fly). G1 rate is 54% — significantly above corpus average, making this one of the performatively tightest decks in the set. Structural architecture is the most sophisticated in the corpus: 6 labeled sections with internal sub-sections, creating a complete arc from innocence through betrayal, self-confrontation, and post-identity void.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: KOMING-OF-AGE WRESTLING ALL-STARS – Growing Up, Booked as Blood Sport (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Can you name the exact afternoon you stopped being a kid, or did somebody quietly swap the script while you were still mid-sentence?

This deck refuses to tell you the comforting versions. It will not tell you that you found yourself. It will not tell you the awkward years were a phase you outgrew clean. It will not tell you that the people who clapped when you debuted the new you were a real crowd instead of an indifferent one waiting for the next act. Growing up is a worked match nobody warned you was worked, and most of the damage came from believing your own gimmick a few years too long. 48 cards, zero false hope, every humiliating rite of passage racked as a fighter you can finally look in the eye.

This is Social Story Wrestling for the years that made you and the years that wrecked you. You do not read a card about The Shattered Kayfabe and nod along. You become him for ninety seconds, the moment the act stopped fooling even you, and let the table decide whether you sold the heartbreak or got booed back behind the curtain.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Koming-of-Age Core Deck: 48 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Confetti Cannon of Lies, the celebration fired in your face to cover the exit, The Indifferent Audience, the crowd that was never actually watching you grow, and The Shattered Kayfabe, the day the performance broke and you saw the wires.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the MANIC, RAGE, and KRAZY modes that decide how hard a given scene is allowed to hurt.
- The Six-Stage Arc: the engine runs the whole crucible in order, from innocence through betrayal and self-confrontation down to the post-identity void, so one session can start a player laughing and leave them quiet.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make decks for people who survived growing up and never got to say the damage out loud at a table that would actually listen. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it. Cut it, play it, hand The Indifferent Audience to whoever still performs for them. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the rules.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
You never found yourself. You picked a fighter and learned to sell the gimmick. Pick a better one.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
